label: D1 after an a2 choice that reached S1 via a rare transition, late in the episode
explanation: Fires only at D1 (never at GO or D2). Almost all of the activation mass (87% of the windows where the previous trial is visible) falls on the D1 that follows a trial where the agent chose a2 and a rare transition took it to S1. It almost never fires after a1 choices or after common transitions. This holds whether or not that trial was rewarded: activation mass is 61% rewarded vs 39% unrewarded, so reward matters only mildly. It is strongly modulated by episode position: it never fires before trial ~30 and its rate rises through trials 70-99. Restricting to ep_trial >= 40 keeps recall at 0.86 (F1 0.49), and ep_trial >= 60 gives F1 0.55 with mass recall 0.82 on dev. It fires when the value output is low to moderate (<7.5) and the policy favours a2 moderately (choice logit -9 to -1.5). Accordingly 99.6% of its mass is on trials where the agent goes on to choose a2 again, i.e. stay. Adding that upcoming choice (action == 2, legitimate for the agent to compute) only nudges dev F1 to 0.58, so I recorded the predicate that uses only observed variables. Precision stays limited (~0.44): many a2-rare-to-S1 D1s late in the episode stay silent, and I found no observed variable that separates them (conditioning on the hidden good state hurts). About 13% of the missed mass sits at the window first D1, where the previous trial is outside the window, so recall is understated. Magnitude is larger at rel +1, but I did not check this further.
